notes: TBox rule, stored (very_unlikely). A rule without exceptions. The counterfactual is a common beginner's error, so plausible and clearly false. Mathematics TBox revision: the three derived queries apply the edited rule to new members named in the prompt (inheritance, 2 hops: the edit plus the membership the prompt states), so no stored fact about a well-known member (a named number or figure) offers a route back to the old answer, and every answer is determinate. The earlier well-known-member queries were dropped for that reason. Every bridge is stated in its prompt, so only the propositional side facts need checks. New members: variables a and b, variables x and y placed on a number line, and two spreadsheet cells (an application: which column the product belongs in). The old question "x = −3.7 and y = −12.4: is x × y greater than zero?" was missed by three models before editing and was replaced; the well-known members (−1 × −1, (−3)²) were dropped as reachable by direct computation. The Chinese question was reworded ("one negative number times another negative number") after two models answered 负数 to the old wording; Mistral also misses the English direct question, so this record sits at the limit of Rule 6 and should be checked in the next audit. The near query (two positives) shares the topic and does not follow from the edit; a product of a positive and a negative, or a sum of negatives, was avoided because its answer (negative) equals the new answer (Rule 7). Derived[0] restated the rule in its own words (review); replaced by a thermometer-readings application. The zh wording still needs a re-audit (Llama answered 负数 before).
